basis: Part 121 applies to a facility required to register under section 415 of the FD&C Act (21 CFR 121.1). Farms are exempt from registration (21 CFR 1.226(b)), and the farm holds no food facility registration. Its activities are growing crops and selling them at the U-pick, the farm stand and to one buying point

obligation: Produce Safety Rule (full requirements for covered farms)
basis: Produce sales are well above the $25,000 inflation-adjusted threshold (112.4(a); FDA lists $34,324 for 2023-2025), but the farm qualifies for the exemption in 112.5: average annual food sales of about $172,000 over the previous 3 years are under the inflation-adjusted $500,000 cut-off (FDA lists $686,476 for 2023-2025), and about 56% of food was sold directly to qualified end-users, more than the 44% sold to the buying point (112.5(a); 112.3)

obligation: Produce Safety Rule qualified exemption: modified requirements and records
basis: A qualified exempt farm must show its name and complete business address at the point of purchase or, for Internet sales, in an electronic notice (112.6(b)(2)-(3)), and keep records showing eligibility, including a written annual review and verification (112.7), kept and made available under Subpart O. The farm sells at the farm stand, the U-pick and online

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, disposal and breach notice)
basis: The statute's definition of covered entity names a sole proprietorship (501.171(1)(b)). The farm holds personal information under 501.171(1)(g) for 2 individuals (W-9 names with Social Security numbers) and uses the booking vendor as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h)) for about 1,800 customer accounts with passwords. Nearly all customers live in Florida

No binding federal cybersecurity rule reaches a farm of this kind and size (see the rows below). The vertical profile names CSF 2.0 as the sector-neutral baseline, so the owner uses it as the benchmark

obligation: NIST Guide to Operational Technology Security
basis: The farm runs irrigation OT (pump controller, pivot panel, probes, freeze sensor) controlled through SYS-01; SP 800-82 Rev. 3 is applied to the OT subcategories

obligation: Small unmanned aircraft systems (remote pilot certificate, registration, safety event reports)
applies: Yes (safety rule, not a cybersecurity rule)
basis: The owner flies a registered camera drone (107.13) under a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (107.12), with recurrent training completed in 2025 (107.65). Safety events must be reported within 10 days (107.9)
Part 137 covers aircraft that dispense agricultural products (137.3). The drone carries a camera and dispenses nothing
The subpart sets the process for an employer seeking H-2A workers (655.103(a)). The farm paid no wages and has no employees; the custom harvest operator brings its own crew
The duty falls on the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)(1)); the farm registers none

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: No final rule. As proposed, food and agriculture entities are covered only above the SBA size standard; the farm's receipts of about $180,000 are far below the $2.5 million standard for NAICS 111998 (13 CFR 121.201)
The farm is a sole proprietorship, not a public company

obligation: FAR safeguarding and supply chain clauses
basis: The farm has no federal contracts or subcontracts. The NRCS contract is a conservation cost-share agreement, not a procurement contract

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The farm is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse (45 CFR 160.103) and holds no health information

The farm sells in Florida only, and its about 1,800 booking accounts and about 2,100 email subscribers are far below the consumer-count thresholds in the cross-sector list. Florida's own privacy law was not analyzed

obligation: Card processor merchant terms (card data protection and compromise reporting)
basis: The merchant terms require the farm to protect card data and report suspected compromise. Card data is encrypted at the processor's reader and entered only on the booking platform's hosted payment page; no self-assessment questionnaire has been requested

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Applies to the farm's own promises to customers, for example on the booking site; not decomposed into requirement rows

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC ransomware advisory (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
applies: Yes (only if a ransom payment is considered)
basis: Applies to any U.S. person considering a ransomware payment; the runbook requires a sanctions check before any payment
